unclustered.title: What if the RSA rumors are true?
unclustered.summary: I recently heard two very alarming rumors. The first is that an internal AI model at one of the big labs has found a weakness in RSA, the encryption scheme behind much of the internet's security. The second is that another model has found a problem in lattice-based cryptography (specifically with ring lwe), that may compromise the post-quantum schemes that were supposed to replace RSA.If these rumors are true, they have potentially disastrous consequences. They would make the internet far less useable for anything serious, which is basically anything that involves money or secrets. Much of the internet's security would need to be replaced, some previously recorded traffic could be decrypted, and we would lose our main fallback against quantum computers.Even if the big labs manage to keep the details of the rumored weaknesses secret, open-weights models will likely be capable enough to find them within a year or two. unclustered.headline: Rumor: AI Model Found RSA Encryption Weakness

Transcript: Building an Early Warning System for Pandemics: "2% of words and <1% of ideas." Cheesy Apple Potato Fritters: "2% of words and 3% of ideas."
